brief:
Today, 6 November, is Legs B at the New York gym. Two nights landed since the last review: Push B on 4 November and Pull B on 5 November, both done in full, every set on the card. That is the first time one set of machines has been run twice, and almost every lift moved: chest press 135 for 10, then 150 for 10, 10; shoulder press 50 lb for 8s (you pressed 50 for 10s and 55 for 8, 9 at Chennai, so that is a hold, not a gain); close pulldown 127.5 for 10, 10; straight-arm pulldown 45 for 12, 12, 12; chest-supported row up to 60; reverse curl 32.5 for 12, 12.

The program stays at version 7. Two things that were on watch are settled by what you did: the reverse pec deck was logged on 4 November (90 for 13, 13, 13), so it stays on Push B, and the fourth shrug set was done on 5 November (80 for 16 on all four), so it stays. Changing nothing else is the decision: eight nights on one set of machines, and the weeks that came out low were the ones with nights missing, not sets that were too hard.

Tonight, Legs B, 20 sets, in pounds. Barbell RDL: 135 for 8, 165 for 8, 180 for 8; it has not been run at New York yet, so these are starting numbers, and 180 for 10 on the top set would earn 190. Smith squat: 95 for 8, three sets, a starting number too; if the smith is taken again, log what you do instead, as you did on 30 October. Leg press: 180 for 12, then 200 for 10, 10. Leg curl: 135 for 12, 150 for 11, 11. Ab wheel: 10, 10, stopping when your lower back starts to arch. Cable crunch: 52.5 for 12, three sets. Calf press: 280 for 12, then 300 for 12, 12. Cue: the RDL and squat sets only count toward progress if they are logged as you go.

After tonight comes Push A, then Pull A. The dated decisions that remain: abs and calves on 8 November, after tonight’s Legs B; the counting rule for the muscles that read over their targets only through half credit, the seated row’s fourth set, the machine lateral raise and the last Push B slot on 9 November.

Three questions are still open. First, the last Push B slot: you logged “Overhead db press” again on 4 November, 50 for 12, 12, but the second set was typed in about 27 hours after the first, so it is from memory. One word in the note, “triceps” or “press”, says what it is. Second, whether New York’s machines are the ones you used in August (the log has no gym before 22 September): “same” or “different” in a note. If they are the same, the seated row, pec deck and leg extension are still below August at the same weight. Third, the crunch on Legs A read “Plank” on 3 November; I do not know whether you chose it or ran out of time, and a timed hold is not on the card unless you ask.

Your logs since 28 October are stamped Meso 3, weeks 5 and 6 (28 to 31 October week 5, 2 to 5 November week 6), while the calendar puts you in week 2 of the restarted block, so if the phase tag at the top of the app is locked, the deload on 25 November will not start by itself; “Automatic (by date)” clears it. No bodyweight is logged since 23 August (207 lb). Conditioning: the build block allows 2 to 3 low-intensity sessions of 20 to 30 minutes a week; the log has none since 21 July, and nothing extra is asked of you tonight.

block.why: Today is the third day of week 2 of 4 in the block restarted on 28 October at the New York gym; it builds to 24 November, deload runs 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, and the show is 115 days away. Two nights landed since yesterday’s review, Push B on 4 November (20 of 20 sets) and Pull B on 5 November (21 of 21), so eight nights in nine days (28, 29, 30, 31 October, 2, 3, 4 and 5 November) have run 149 of the 162 sets the current program asks for, counting what you did in place of a slot. The 13 missing sets are mostly two nights, Legs B on 30 October (14 of 20) and Push B on 31 October (17 of 20), plus one set each short on Push A 28 October (smith incline 3 of 4), Pull B 29 October (shrug 3 of 4) and two on Legs A 3 November (the crunch slot became one plank); the two newest nights lost nothing. This is the first week where the second pass at New York has numbers to compare, and it is working: chest press 135 for 12 to 150 for 10, shoulder press 45 to 50, close pulldown 127.5 for 9 to 10, straight-arm pulldown 45 for 9 to 12, shrug 80 for 15 to 16, reverse curl 32.5 for 10 to 12. Two held-back watches closed on the logs, the pec deck (kept) and the fourth shrug set (kept). Nothing in the program changes today. Seven of the eight lifts the dossier calls stalled compare machines across gyms, August nights with no gym, or a plank against crunches; the Pull A deadlift is up, not flat (225 for 6, 235 for 5, 240 for 5 across 8 October, 23 October and 2 November, and still under August’s numbers), and it has one New York visit. Rotating after one repeat at a gym would throw away the baseline this restart was made to build. Legs B is the one night that has not had its first New York pass: the barbell RDL and smith squat have never run in their own slots, so tonight’s numbers are starting numbers. The leg-night order stays: Legs A ends on the crunch and Legs B ends on the calf press, so if the last slot is what gets cut, calves still get Legs A and abs still get Legs B. The four-week averages in the muscle lines read lower than current training because the window still holds the week of 19 October, with no chest, triceps or quads, and the deload days. Every “a week done” figure counts half credit from compound lifts, so compare it with the number on paper, not the direct count. Dated: abs and calves 8 November, the counting rule, the fourth row set, the machine lateral raise and the last Push B slot 9 November. Next boundary is the deload on 25 November; the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.
